blocks.text: Part VI of the Constitution is divided into 6 chapter.
Chapter I: General (Definition) (Art 152)
Chapter II: The State Executive (Governor + CM + CoM + Advocate General) (Art 153-167)
Chapter III: The State Legislature (Art 168-212)
Chapter IV: Legislative Power of the Governor (Art 213)
Chapter V: The High Courts in the States (Art 214 - 231)
Chapter VI: Subordinate Courts (Art 233 - 237)
Article Mapping from Union to State level:
Articles 73-111 (Parliament) Add 89— gives corresponding articles of State Legislature.
Articles 112-213 — Add 90 — Gives Corresponding articles for State Legislature.
Key Replacements: President > Governor
Parliament — State Legislature
Prime Minister > Chief Minister
Council of Ministers (Union) + Council of Ministers (State)
Attorney General of India > Advocate General of State
Consolidated Fund of India > Consolidated Fund of State Chapter II: State Executive (Articles 153-167)
Consists of (Governor + CM + CoM + Advocate General)
Article 153: Governor of States
There shall be a Governor for each State.
7th Constitutional Amendment allowed for the appointment of same person as the Governor of two or more states.
Article 154: Executive Power of State
Executive power of State vests in the Governor.
Can be exercised directly or through subordinate officers.
Article 155: Appointment of Governor
Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
Article 156: Term of Office of Governor
156(1) Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
156(2) Governor may, address his resignation to the President 156(3) Term: 5years from the date of assuming office, subject to earlier removal or resignation.
Article 157: Qualifications for Appointment as Governor
Must be a Citizen of India and should have completed 35 years of age.
Article 158: Conditions of Governor's Office 158(1) Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or State Legislature; must vacate seat before entering office.
158(2) Governor cannot hold any office of profit.
158(3) Governor is entitled to use official residence without rent; emoluments and privileges as determined by the Parliament.
158(3A) If serving multiple states,emoluments are shared as per Presidential order.
158(4) Emoluments and allowances cannot be reduced during his tenure.
Article 159: Oath or Affirmation by Governor
Oath administered by Chief Justice of High Court, or in. absence, senior-most judge.
Article 160: Discharge of Governor's functions in contingencies
President can appoint a person to discharge functions of Governor during contingencies.
Article 161: Power of Governor to Grant Pardons
Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, or commute sentences.
But he cannot:
Pardon death sentence (only President can).
Use pardoning power against Martial Court sentences.
Article 162: Extent of Executive Power of State
State's executive power extends to matters on which the State Legislature can make laws.
Article 163: Council of Ministers to Aid and Advise Governor 163(1): Council of Ministers, headed by Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor.
Advice of Council of Ministers is not binding on the Governor and Governor can act on his discretion in certain situations.
163(2): If a question arises regarding whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion,the Governor's decision is final and cannot be questioned.
Article 164: Other Provisions as to Ministers 164(1) Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor; other Ministers appointed on CM's advice.
164(2) Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state.
164(3) Ministers must take oaths of office and secrecy as administered by the Governor.
164(4) A Minister who is not elected as MLA/MLC within 6 consecutive months ceases to be a Minister.
164(5) Salaries and allowances determined by State Legislature.

164(6) In a hung assembly, where no single party holds a majority, the Governor uses circumstantial discretion to appoint a Chief Minister, typically selecting the leader most likely to command a majority.
Areiele 165: Advocate General for the State 165(1) Appointed by Governor; must be qualified to be a High Court judge.
165(2) Advises State Government on legal matters.
165(3) Holds office till the Governor's pleasure.
Article 166: Conduct of Business of State Government All executive actions must be expressed in the name of Governor.
Article 167: Duties of Chief Minister
Communicate decisions of Council of Ministers to Governor.
Chapter III: State Legislature (Articles 168-212)
Article 168: Constitution of Legislatures in States (1) Every State shall have a Legislature, consisting of the Governor.
Upper House/ Permanent House
All states have a Legislative Assembly. (Unicameral legislature)
6 States have a Legislative Council as well. (Bicameral legislature), they are:
Sy Ape K - Karnataka A - Andhra Pradesh
Telangana B - Bihar
Maharashtra U - Uttar Pradesh —
Karnataka M - Maharashtra
[3 UTs out of 8 have LA, i.e. Delhi, Puducherry, JéK. · Article 169: Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils
Parliament can create or abolish Legislative Councils just by Simple Majority, based on a resolution passed by the State Legislative Assembly by Special Majority.
Such a law is not considered an amendment under Article 368.
Article 170: Composition of Legislative Assemblies 170(1) Legislative Assembly: not less than 60 and not more than 500 members should be elected by direct election.
170(2) Constituencies should have roughly equal population- seat ratio.
Special case: Goa, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim > Minimum 30 members.

Mizoram — 40 members; Nagaland > 46 members Article 171: Composition of Legislative Councils 171(1) Total members shall not exceed 1/3rd of Legislative Assembly, minimum 40 members. (Indirectly Elected)
171(2) Of the total no. members of the LC of a state:
(a) 1/3rd elected by members of local authorities (municipalities, district boards, etc.).
(b) 1/12th elected by Graduates of 3 years or more.
(c) 1/12th elected by Teachers with at least 3 years experience (d) 1/3rd elected by Legislative Assembly members.

(e) 1/6th nominated by Governor (experts in literature, science, art, social service) — Li SAS + Cooperative movement Article 172: Duration of State Legislatures 172(1) Legislative Assembly term=5 years from first meeting, unless dissolved earlier.
172(2) Legislative Council: Permanent body; 1/3rd members retire every 2 years. (Hence, term of a member = 6 years)
Article 173: Qualifications for Membership (a) Must be a citizen of India.
(b) Minimum 25 years for Legislative Assembly, 30 years for Legislative Council.
(c) Must possess other qualifications prescribed by Parliament.
Article 174: Sessions, Prorogation, Dissolution 174(1) Governor summons house of the Legislature;maximum gap between two sessions is 6 months.
174(2) Governor can: (a) Prorogue Houses or
(b) Dissolve Legislative Assembly.
Article 175: Governor's Address and Messages Governor may address and send message to Legislative Assembly or Council or both houses assembled together.
Article 176: Special Address by the Governor
At the commencement of first session after each general elections and the first session of each year, Governor addresses Legislature.
Article 177: Rights of Ministers and Advocate General
Ministers and Advocate General can participate in debates and proceedings but cannot vote if they are not a member of the House.
Article 178: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Legislative Assembly.
Legislative Assembly elects a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.
Article 179: Vacation and Resignation or Removal of Speaker/ Deputy Speaker.
To be done by resolution passed by majority of the Assembly members.
Article 180: Duties of Deputy Speaker
Deputy Speaker acts as the Speaker when office is vacant or Speaker is absent.
Article 181: Speaker/Deputy Speaker not to preside during consideration of resolution for their own removal.
Article 182: Chairman and Deputy Chairman of Legislative Council.
Article 183: Vacation, Resignation, Removal of Chairman / Deputy Chairman
Similar to provisions for Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
Article 184: Duties of Deputy Chairman
Deputy Chairman acts as Chairman when office is vacant or chairman is absent.
Article 185: Chairman or Deputy Chairman shall not preside when his removal resolution is being considered.
Article 186: Salaries and Allowances of Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman, Deputy Chairman
Salaries and allowances are determined by State Legislature.
Article 187: Secretariat of State Legislature
Appointed and regulated by State Legislature.
Article 188: Oath or Affirmation by Members Article 189: Voting in Houses, Vacancies, and Quorum 189(1) All questions in Legislature decided by majority of members present and voting.
189(2) The presiding officer does not vote in the first instance.
He/she only has a casting vote in case of a tie, same rule as Parliament (Article 100). form.
189(3) Legislature can act despite vacancies.
189(4) Quorum for a meeting = 10% of total membership.
Article 190: Vacation of Seats
Seat vacated if:
a person is member of both the houses, e member resigns,
a member becomes subject to disqualification Article 191: Disqualifications of Membership Disqualification if:
Holds office of profit.
Disqualified under anti-defection laws or other Parliament-made laws.
Article 192: Decision on Disqualification Article 193: Penalty for Sitting and Voting before taking Oath or when disqualified: fine decided by Legislature.
Article 194: Powers, Privileges, and Immunities of State Legislatures and Their Members Article 195: Salaries and Allowances of Members Article 196: Introduction and Passing of Bills
Bills can originate in either House (if bicameral).
Bill must be passed by both Houses and assented by Governor to become a law.
In case of an Ordinary bill, Legislative Assembly has upper hand over Legislative Council.
When a bill originates in the LC, and if LA disagrees, then the bill lapses, and there is no provision for joint sitting in Part VI.
What happens when a bill originates in LA—two cases:
1. LA —LC —• Governor
2. LA ——e · CY — Governor
In 2nd case, LC can only delay an Ordinary Bill by maximum 4 months i.e. 3 months in first instance and for 1 month in 2nd instance.
Article 197: Restriction on Powers of Legislative Council as to bills other than Money bill Article 198: Special Procedure for Money Bills
Money Bill can be introduced only in Legislative Assembly.

Then sent to Legislative Council for recommendations, LC cannot reject the bill, it must return the bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations, if the council fails to do so, the money bill is deemed passed in its original Article 199: Definition of Money Bill Article 200: Assent to Bills by the Governor
Under Article 200 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor has the following four options when a bill is presented:
1. Assent to the Bill: The Governor may give assent, and the bill becomes an Acct.
2. Withhold Assent: The Governor may refuse assent, and the bill fails.
3. Return the Bill (if not a Money Bill): The Governor may return the bill to the State Legislature for reconsideration.
If passed again, the Governor is bound to give assent.
4. Reserve the Bill for the President: The Governor may reserve the bill for consideration of the President, especially in certain cases of constitutional importance.

Article 201: Bills Reserved for President's Consideration State of Tamil Nadu vs Governor of Tamil Nadu (April 2025): The Supreme Court of India held that indefinite delay by the Governor in acting on Bills is illegal and prescribed timelines for decision-making. It also observed that the President should decide on Bills reserved under Article 201 within a period of three months.
Article 202: Annual Financial Statement (Budget)
Article 203: Procedure in Legislature with Respect to Estimates
Demands for grants made only on the recommendation of the Governor.
Article 204: Appropriation Bills
Article 205: Supplementary, Additional, and Excess Grants Article 206: Votes on Account, Votes of Credit, and Exceptional Grants.
Article 207: Special Provisions for Financial Bills Money Bills require prior recommendation of the Governor for introduction.
Article 208: Rules of Procedure

Article 209: Regulation of Procedure Relating to Financial Business Article 210: Language to be used in the Legislature Article 211: Restriction on Discussion in the legislature Article 212: Courts not to Inquire into Legislature Proceedings Article 213: Power of Governor to Promulgate Ordinances during Recess of the legislature Article 214-231: High Courts Article 233-237: Subordinate Courts Official Language - Part X VII (Articles 343-351)
1. Language of the Union (Art. 343-344)
Article 343: Official language of the Union - Hindi in Devanagari script

It allowed English to continue for all official purposes for 15 years from 1950, with Parliament authorized to extend this use further — English continued via Official Languages Act, 1963 Article 344: Commission and Committee of parliament in official language.
President constitute Official Language Commission whose recommendations would be non-binding.
The first Official Language Commission under Article 344 was headed by B. G. Kher (1955)
2. Regional Languages (Article 345-347)
Article 345: Official language of state.
State can adopt: Any regional language or Hindi
English continues till then
Article 346: Official language for communication between States and Union.
Article 347: Special provision relating to language spoken by a section of population.
President can recognize language of a section of population 3. Language of Judiciary (Article 348-349)
Article 348: Language of Supreme court, High courts and Bills.

All Proceedings, Bills & Acts should be in English -• Governor of a state may, with the prior consent of the President, authorize the use of Hindi or another official state language in High Court proceedings.
Article 349: Special Procedure for enactment of laws relating to language.
Language-related laws need: President's prior sanction (for first 15 years)
4. Special Directives (Article 350-351
Article 350: Languages to be used in Representation for redress of Grievances.
Any language used by Govt. is allowed
350A: Facilities for instructions in mother tongue at primary stage.
Added through 7th CA 1956.
Primary education in mother tongue (linguistic minorities)
350B: Special Officer for linguistic minorities.
Added through 7th CA 1956
Article 351: Directives for Development of Hindi Language.
